original_card.question: Can a changed query demand or caller remove real work while satisfying native chronology and restoration?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

actual_scope: On the paired-star contract, consecutive stage halves with no thin map between them need total thin rank at least q*g. At g=31 and q=26, five rank-26 maps are short of that bound.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks about a changed query demand. The assigned question is the open g=31, q=26 paired-star profile from Discussion #5593 and research/coupled31-chronology, restricted to consecutive halves. The g=13, q=8 profile is a different assignment and is not claimed.
bottleneck_link: Side result relative to the selected frontier. The profile passes the paired-star chronological rank floor and is unconstructed. This note removes only the consecutive-halves schedule. It supplies no supplier and no kappa change.
stop_rule: Stop after the consecutive-halves identity and the rank comparison are checked. Do not search nested orders or claim unrestricted nonexistence.

open_questions.question: Can a thin map between the two halves of a stage meet the g=31, q=26 endpoint with total thin rank 130?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That placement is the remaining consecutive-block escape. A yes would be a witness under a wider schedule. A no would extend this obstruction.
open_questions.first_step: Compute the core-to-leaf coefficient of one internal gap in the eigenbasis of that stage, with the off-diagonal blocks free, and test whether rank-q maps can supply I_52.
open_questions.blocked_by: The scalar prefix used here is false while a stage is open. No internal-gap identity is proved. The g=3 finite censuses are a different profile.

open_questions.question: Can nested or crossing stage intervals with noncommuting projectors meet the g=31, q=26 endpoint with five rank-26 maps?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Those orders are outside the adjacency hypothesis, so the profile can still exist there.
open_questions.first_step: Check the pure product of one crossed pair and one nested pair in the same projector algebra before any q=26 search.
open_questions.blocked_by: Adjacency is required to replace a stage by D*I and D*T. No witness and no all-order argument for those intervals is supplied.
